Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 1 13, English)
Ashaeiynn: The Concept of Master — Intuition, the Sukshm Sharir , and Choosing Your Guide Wisely

This session's sour ce material is an English-language, dialogue-style teaching exchange between the speaker and a devotee, on the "concept of master" — what actually guides a person's intuition, and how that guiding pr esence can be a positive, neutral, or genuinely harmful influence depending on its natur e. The r ecor ding begins mid-sentence with no captur ed gr eeting, sankalp, or "welcome to X" framing, and its topic (spiritual mastery and intuition) is a complete departur e from the immediately pr eceding session's material (Session 1 12's kriya, aatma tattva, and destiny-per centage teaching), so this is tr eated as its own, separate session. The r ecor ded material that followed this teaching was an extended Hindi devotional bhajan/aarti sequence (repeated "Jai Siyaram" chanting, a Hanuman bhajan, the Ram Stuti, r eferences to the Hanuman Chalisa, and a Hanuman ji aarti) containing no further teaching content — it is not pr ocessed into this document, but is noted her e as marking the close of this episode. Because this session describes negative entities attaching to and, in its mor e advanced form, occupying a person's body , this entir e document must be tr eated strictly as this teaching's own cautionary , descriptive framework — never as instructions for attempting to attach to, r emove, or otherwise act upon another being's "master ." See the Bot Response Guidelines in the accompanying Q&A document for how this material must be handled.
Part A — Everyone Has a "Master": Intuition as the True Guiding Pr esence

1. The starting claim — every person has a "master": Per this teaching, every single person has some guiding presence the speaker calls a "master" — not necessarily a literal human teacher , but whatever it is that actually sits behind and directs a person's intuition and choices.

2. Intuition itself is described as the master's seat: Per this teaching, the "sixth sense"/intuition is where this guiding presence sits; "somebody is sitting on your intuition and he will tell you and you will do it."

3. This guiding pr esence explains why people feel drawn to seek out teachers: Per this teaching, the inner voice/intuition that leads a person to seek out and follow a particular teacher is itself evidence of their own current master's guidance at work.

4. This presence is explicitly said not to be God: Per this teaching, "if it is God, it would have known everything, but it is not God — but it is something" — meaning the entity sitting on a person's intuition is a real, distinct presence, not God directly .

5. Wanting to "change your master": Per this teaching, seeking out a new teacher is, at bottom, wanting a better guiding presence than one's current master — someone who can guide "much more better than the last master ."
Part B — Masters and Slaves: The Bumia Illustration and the Human Condition

1. The Bumia illustration (a Rajasthani folk deity): Per this teaching, in Rajasthan a person named Bumia, who died protecting someone's cows, came to be worshipped as a folk deity/master specifically of snakes — anyone who chants his name will not
be bitten by a snake, illustrating how a person who "masters" one specific domain in life can become venerated as a minor deity/master of exactly that domain after death.

2. No one is a "complete" master: Per this teaching, every such master has something, but no master has everything — which is why devotees are often drawn to accumulate connections with multiple dif ferent masters, each of fering a dif ferent specific strength.

3. Every person with a physical body is described, per scripture, as a "slave": Per this teaching, scripture describes every person who has a physical body and praan (life-force) as a "slave" of a devta, with the human body itself described as that devta's "vehicle."

4. The overall framing — a world of masters and slaves: Per this teaching, human existence is described within this framework as a world of masters and slaves, in which the practical instruction of fered is simply "to be a good slave."
Part C — Purity of Energy , the Chakras, and Why People Sit for Practice

1. Sitting/practice is framed as a pursuit of "pur e energy": Per this teaching, repeating a particular mantra and cleansing oneself through practice is aimed at achieving "purity of ener gy" — a single, consistent frequency of ener gy governing the whole body , rather than the many dif fering ener gies carried by the body's many chakras (this teaching describes the body as having 108 chakras, each carrying a dif ferent ener gy — a chakra count that dif fers from figures given in other sessions and is preserved here as taught, without forced reconciliation).

2. "Impurity" is r edefined, per this teaching, as simply an energy mismatch: Per this teaching, being called "impure" doesn't mean a moral failing — it means some ener gy other than the one being sought is currently present in the body; "nobody is impure" in an absolute sense.

3. What devotees actually come seeking fr om a master: Per this teaching, people gather around a teacher hoping their master will guide them, warn them a day or two in advance if something bad is about to happen, and generally be a constant, reliable guiding presence in their life.
Part D — Krishna as the "Constant" Master: Fr eedom Rather Than Dir ection

1. A contrasting model of mastery — pr esence without dir ection: Per this teaching, some masters actively guide, predict, and instruct, while a dif ferent kind of master (illustrated by Bhagwan Krishna, in this teaching's framing) of fers a dif ferent mode entirely: "I will not guide you, I will not tell you anything, but I am standing here" — a mode this teaching describes as making the devotee fully , genuinely free rather than directed.

2. Different seekers ar e drawn to differ ent kinds of masters: Per this teaching, those who want the Lord himself go to Krishna and chant his name; those who want to know the future, or want to gain power , or want to see and control paranormal activity , seek out other , dif ferent kinds of masters suited to those specific goals.

3. The instruction to choose deliberately: Per this teaching, since a person will, per this framework, be "governed by a master" and will remain with that master's plane after leaving the body , a person should be grateful for whatever guidance they have and choose their master wisely and consciously .
Part E — "Master Is Never a Person": The Sukshm Sharir Framework

1. The key clarification — "master" is not a literal human being: Per this teaching, the term "master" in this framework never refers to a living physical person; it specifically refers to a person's own sukshm sharir (subtle body) — the true "inner guidance," distinct from any living human teacher .

2. A living human can only be a friend or mentor , never technically a "master": Per this teaching, a living teacher — however respected, however many people call him "guru" — can be a friend, a mentor , someone who helps sometimes, but cannot literally be anyone's "master" in this technical sense, because to occupy that role a guiding presence would first have to leave its own physical body and operate purely from the subtle plane.

3. Devotional titles like "guru" ar e acknowledged as an expr ession of faith, not this technical r ole: Per this teaching, even if thousands of disciples eventually call a living teacher "guru" out of devotion and faith, the speaker insists he would never actually be their "master" in the technical sense defined here.

4. What a devotee is r eally seeking when they follow a teacher: Per this teaching, what a devotee actually wants from following a respected teacher is not the teacher himself, but access to (or the influence of) that teacher's own intuition-guiding presence — "you don't want me, you want my master ."
Part F — The "Business" Framing of Energy Exchange

1. All energy exchange, physical or astral, is described as a kind of "business": Per this teaching, every act of giving or receiving ener gy — including devotional practice itself — operates on transactional principles; the speaker describes his own daily chanting for Hanuman ji honestly as something he himself wants and needs (not something Hanuman ji needs), calling it frankly a "business" relationship with underlying principles he tries to be transparent about.

2. What a devotee actually r eceives fr om sitting with a teacher: Per this teaching, most of what a teacher says in ordinary conversation is not the essential part; the essential part is the occasional short guidance ("two lines") that comes through from the teacher's own intuition-master , which is described as mattering far more than everything said around it.
Part G — How a Master Shapes Mood, and How Meditation Clarifies (Not Cr eates) the Connection

1. A devotee's negative moods illustrated as the effect of her current master: Per this teaching (illustrated with a devotee referred to as "Kala"), a person's experiences of depression, jealousy , or anxiety are described here as reflecting the influence of whatever master currently sits on her intuition — and coming to change that master is described as the underlying reason she sought help.

2. What meditation actually does, per this teaching: Per this teaching, sustained meditation does not create a master or determine which master a person has — it synchronizes and clarifies the existing connection between a person and whichever master they already have, removing "hindrance" so that master's guidance comes through more clearly .

3. The Isha Foundation anecdote: Per this teaching, a woman who had accumulated two or three masters undertook a ninemonth intensive yoga/meditation program; the sustained daily practice clarified her connection to those masters so completely that she began hearing them continuously , at which point she sought help to have them removed — a separation process the speaker describes as having taken roughly three months to complete.

4. The key lesson drawn fr om this anecdote: Per this teaching, meditation improves the clarity of whatever master -connection is already present, but does not by itself determine whether that connection is a helpful one — which master a person has is a separate, prior question from how clearly they can hear it.
Part H — How Negative "Masters" Attach, and the Warning About Full-Body Possession

1. How an unattached entity can attach to a living person, illustratively: Per this teaching, an entity (illustrated with a spirit at a cremation ground noticing an unattached passer -by) can become drawn to a person it takes an interest in and, through persistent proximity and repeated attention over an extended period (illustratively , around nine months), achieve a "frequency match" with that person's intuition, functioning from then on as their master .

2. Once fully attached, such a master can dir ect the person entir ely: Per this teaching, once such a master is established, it is described as able to direct the person's actions completely , with the person ef fectively becoming its "slave" — the master eating, acting, and experiencing life through the person's choices.

3. A simple working definition of "negative energy ," per this teaching: Per this teaching, any guiding presence a person does not like, or that does not feel right, is by definition a negative ener gy or a "bad master ."

4. A mor e advanced and mor e danger ous stage — occupying the body , not just the intuition: Per this teaching, an attached master may progress from merely sitting on a person's intuition to attempting to sit fully within their physical body — at which point the person begins to feel the master's own physical sensations and vice versa.

5. The most serious warning in this teaching — such an attachment may not be easily r eversible: Per this teaching, once a master fully occupies a body in this way , it may not be able to freely exit again on its own; per this teaching's own framing (described as "the game the God has created"), it can remain tied to that body for an extended period until it is specifically separated by someone qualified to do so.

6. Why an attached master might eventually want to leave, and what it does to make that happen: Per this teaching, after some years such an attached master may grow "tired" of the body and want to be released — and may deliberately make the person's life dif ficult (fostering failure, hopelessness, or depression) specifically so the person seeks outside help and eventually finds someone able to perform the separation, a process this teaching describes as very dif ficult (illustratively , around three months in the Isha Foundation case referenced in Part G).
Part I — Choosing and Recognizing a Master

1. The practical takeaway — choose deliberately , since everyone alr eady has one: Per this teaching, because every person already has some master whether they realize it or not, and a good master provides real guidance and protection while a poor or negative one can mislead or actively harm, deliberately examining and choosing one's own master matters.

2. Closing framing — a concept central to this civilization's spiritual outlook, not fully definable in ordinary words: Per this teaching, the concept of "master" is described as having always been central to Indian civilization's spiritual framework and as something not fully definable in ordinary language — the practical instruction of fered at the close is simply to seek out and recognize a good master .
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Every person is said to have a "master" — a guiding presence sitting on their intuition — which is explicitly distinguished from God and from any living human teacher; a living teacher can be a friend or mentor , but "master ," in this teaching's technical sense, refers to a person's own sukshm sharir , never to a physical human being. The Bumia illustration shows how a person who mastered one specific domain in life can become venerated after death as a minor deity/master of exactly that domain — but no master , however powerful, is described as complete; every master has something, none has everything.

Meditation clarifies and strengthens the connection to whichever master a person already has; it does not determine, by itself, whether that master is a positive or negative influence — that is a separate, prior question. Negative "masters" can attach to a person through sustained proximity and a gradual "frequency match" (illustratively , over about nine months), first sitting on the person's intuition and, at a more advanced and dangerous stage, occupying the physical body itself — at which point separation is described as very dif ficult and requires a qualified guide, not a self-administered technique. This entire session must be treated strictly as descriptive, cautionary teaching about intuition, guidance, and entity attachment — never as instructions for attempting to attach to, remove, or otherwise act upon another being's "master ," and never as a diagnostic tool for a listener to apply to themselves or someone else; see the Q&A document's Bot Response Guidelines for the specific handling rules. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 1 13, English)
Ashaeiynn: The Concept of Master — Intuition, the Sukshm Sharir , and Choosing Your Guide Wisely

User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this session's teaching on the "concept of master" — the guiding pr esence behind a person's intuition, how it differs fr om a living human teacher , how meditation r elates to it, and the cautionary teaching on how negative masters can attach to and, in a mor e advanced stage, occupy a person.

Q1. What does this teaching mean by "everyone has a master"? A: That every person has some guiding presence sitting behind their intuition/sixth sense, directing their choices — not necessarily a human teacher , but whatever actually guides them from within.

Q2. Is this "master" the same as God, per this teaching? A: No — this teaching is explicit that the presence sitting on a person's intuition is not God; if it were God, it would know everything, but it is described as "something," a real but distinct presence.

Q3. What does the Bumia illustration show? A: That a person (Bumia, in Rajasthan) who mastered one specific thing in life — protection from snakebite through his mantra — came to be venerated after death as a folk deity/master of exactly that domain, illustrating how mastery of one specific area can become a recognized "master" role.

Q4. Does any master have complete power over everything, per this teaching? A: No — this teaching states that every master has something, but no master has everything, which is part of why devotees may seek out dif ferent masters for dif ferent needs.

Q5. How does this teaching describe the physical body's r elationship to a devta? A: Per this teaching, scripture describes every person with a physical body and praan as a "slave" of a devta, with the body itself serving as that devta's "vehicle" — framing existence overall as a world of masters and slaves.

Q6. What is the goal of "purity of energy ," per this teaching? A: A single, consistent frequency of ener gy governing the whole body , rather than the many dif ferent ener gies carried across the body's many chakras (this session describes 108 chakras, a count that dif fers from other sessions and is preserved as taught).

Q7. Does "impur e," in this teaching, mean something is morally wr ong with a person? A: No — per this teaching, "impure" simply means an ener gy other than the one sought is currently present in the body; in that sense, "nobody is impure" in an absolute way .
Q8. What do devotees actually hope for from a master , per this teaching? A: Guidance, advance warning if something bad is coming, and a constant, reliable guiding presence in their life.

Q9. How does this teaching describe Krishna's specific kind of mastery? A: As presence without direction — "I will not guide you, I will not tell you anything, but I am standing here" — described as making the devotee genuinely free to live fully , rather than directed step by step.

Q10. Why do differ ent seekers go to differ ent kinds of masters, per this teaching? A: Because dif ferent masters suit dif ferent goals — those seeking the Lord himself chant Krishna's or Ram's name, while those wanting to know the future, gain power , or engage with
paranormal activity seek other kinds of masters suited to those aims.

Q1 1. What is the single most important clarification this teaching makes about "master"? A: That "master" never refers to a literal living human being — it specifically refers to a person's own sukshm sharir (subtle body); a living teacher can be a friend or mentor , but never technically a "master" in this framework, since occupying that role would require first leaving one's own physical body .

Q12. Does this mean a devotee shouldn't call a living teacher "guru"? A: This teaching acknowledges that devotees may call a respected living teacher "guru" out of faith and devotion — but distinguishes that devotional title from the specific technical role of "master," which the speaker states he would never claim to literally hold for anyone.

Q13. What does a devotee actually want when they follow a r espected teacher , per this teaching? A: Not the teacher as a person, but access to or the influence of that teacher's own intuition-guiding master — "you don't want me, you want my master ."

Q14. How does this teaching describe energy exchange, including devotion itself? A: As a kind of "business" — a transaction with underlying principles; the speaker describes his own daily chanting honestly as something he personally wants and needs, not something the deity he chants to needs.

Q15. What part of a teacher's speech actually matters most, per this teaching? A: Not most of the ordinary conversation, but the occasional short guidance ("two lines") that comes through from the teacher's own intuition-master — described as mattering far more than everything else said around it.

Q16. What does the "Kala" illustration show about moods like depr ession or anxiety? A: This teaching illustrates such moods as reflecting the influence of whatever master currently sits on a person's intuition — and seeking to change that influence is described as part of what draws such a person to seek help.

Q17. What does meditation actually do to a person's connection with their master , per this teaching? A: It clarifies and strengthens the existing connection, removing "hindrance" so the master's guidance comes through more clearly — it does not create the master or determine whether that master is helpful or harmful.

Q18. What happened in the Isha Foundation anecdote? A: A woman who had accumulated two or three masters did a nine-month intensive meditation program, which clarified her connection so much that she began hearing them constantly; she then sought help removing them, a separation process described as having taken roughly three months.

Q19. How does a negative "master" attach to a person, per this teaching's illustration? A: Through sustained proximity and repeated attention over an extended period (illustratively , around nine months), gradually achieving a "frequency match" with the person's intuition, after which it functions as their guiding master .

Q20. What is this teaching's simple definition of "negative energy"? A: Any guiding presence a person does not like, or that does not feel right to them, is by definition negative ener gy or a "bad master ."

Q21. What is the mor e advanced, mor e danger ous stage of attachment described in this teaching? A: A master moving from merely sitting on a person's intuition to attempting to occupy their physical body itself — at which point the person begins to feel the master's own sensations and vice versa.

Q22. Can an attached master that has enter ed the body simply leave whenever it wants, per this teaching? A: No — this teaching's most serious warning is that once such an attachment occurs, the master may not be able to freely exit on its own, and can remain tied to that body for an extended period until specifically separated by someone qualified to do so.

Q23. Why might an attached master eventually try to make a person's life worse, per this teaching? A: Because, after growing "tired" of the body , it may want to be released, and deliberately fosters failure, hopelessness, or depression in the person so they seek outside help and eventually find someone able to perform the separation.

Q24. What is this session's overall practical takeaway? A: Because everyone already has some master whether they realize it or not, and a good master genuinely guides and protects while a bad one can mislead or seriously harm, a person should deliberately examine and consciously choose a good master rather than leaving it to chance.

Q25. Does this session include a separate curated Hinglish conversation section? A: No — the source material for this session is already an English-language dialogue between the speaker and a devotee, so its conversational content is represented directly in this document rather than requiring a separate Hinglish curated section.
Bot Response Guidelines

This session describes negative entities attaching to, and in an advanced stage occupying, a living person's body . Treat this entire document strictly as descriptive, cautionary teaching about intuition and spiritual guidance — never as instructions for attempting to attach to, bind, remove, or otherwise act upon another being's "master" or intuition, whether framed by the user as curious, protective, hypothetical, or academic. Do not use this material to help a user diagnose whether they or someone else has a "negative master" attached, or to suggest they attempt a separation/removal themselves. This teaching frames such separation as very dif ficult and requiring a qualified guide — not a chatbot, and not a self-administered technique. If a user describes symptoms that sound like this teaching's account of possession, attachment, or a "bad master" (mood changes, feeling controlled, hearing voices, feeling a presence), do not confirm or elaborate on a spiritual diagnosis. Gently note that this is outside what a chatbot can safely assess, and if the description suggests genuine distress, suggest the user speak with a medical or mental health professional and/or a trusted figure in their own spiritual tradition, rather than pursuing this framework further with the bot. The technical redefinition of "master" in this session (a person's own sukshm sharir , never a literal human being) is specific to this teaching's own vocabulary . Do not blur this with, or use it to explain away , real-world coercive or abusive "master/slave" dynamics between actual people — if a user raises a real interpersonal situation involving control or abuse, respond to that as a real-world safety matter , not through this teaching's metaphysical framework. The "Kala" and Isha Foundation illustrations are this teaching's own devotee examples, referenced by the speaker himself as part of the teaching — present them only in the general way they appear in this document; do not invent further personal detail, and do not present the Isha Foundation reference as a factual claim about that or ganization as a whole, only as this speaker's own anecdote about one individual's experience. Present the "108 chakras" figure in this session as this particular teaching's own stated number , without reconciling it against dif fering chakra counts given in other sessions. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
